chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us, from Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami, from Mubarak, the servant of al-Rida (peace be upon him), from al-Rida, Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon them both), who said:
A believer will not be a true believer until there are three traits in him: a tradition from his Lord, a tradition from his Prophet, and a tradition from his Leader.

As for the tradition from his Lord, it is the concealment of the secret. Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, said: 'The Knower of the Unseen, and so, He does not disclose, to His (knowledge of the) Unseen, anyone, except for the one He was pleased with of a Messenger' (72:26-27).

As for the tradition from his Prophet, it is conformity with people, for indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, ordered His Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, with regards to conformity with people, and so He said: 'Take (upon yourself to perform) pardoning, enjoin good and look away from the ignorant ones.' (7:199)

As for the tradition from his Leader, it is patience towards suffering and harm. Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, says: 'And those patient towards suffering, harm and during hostilities, those are the ones who were truthful, and those are the godfearing.' (2:177)
ai.seo_question: What are the three essential traits that define a true believer according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a hierarchical model of spiritual refinement, where the believer internalizes divine secrecy, prophetic social grace, and Imami endurance. This triad reflects the Shia emphasis on the continuity of guidance, linking the unseen (ghayb) with visible social conduct and steadfastness under the authority of the Imam. The inclusion of 'concealing secrets' highlights the mystical dimension of faith, while 'patience in adversity' underscores the political and spiritual resilience required of the faithful.
